title: Admin Eyes Only
story:
[RADIO] Kestrel Control, this is Halvorsen. Kip ran a port scan from the crew wifi and found the admin panel on port 9090, wide open to anybody on the station network. It has the door controls and the generator schedule on it. Kip says it "looked like a printer".

The panel is the container `admin-panel`, started last week with a plain `-p 9090:80`. Only a shell on the control machine itself should reach it. Recreate it with the same page and the same read-only mount, but with port 9090 listening on loopback only. Confirm from your side. Halvorsen out.
objectives: Run `admin-panel` from `nginx:alpine` with `/workspace/panel` mounted read-only at `/usr/share/nginx/html`
Publish container port 80 on `127.0.0.1:9090` only (not on `0.0.0.0`)
`http://127.0.0.1:9090/` from the control machine still serves the admin console page
startingState: `admin-panel` is already running but published on every interface (`0.0.0.0:9090`). Its page is in `/workspace/panel`.
hints: A published port can be tied to one host address. The address goes in front of the port numbers in the publish option. A running container's ports cannot be edited, so you will recreate it.
The `-p` syntax is `[host-ip:]host-port:container-port`. Remove the old container first, then start a new one with the same name, the same bind mount and a loopback host-ip.

```bash
docker rm -f admin-panel
docker run -d --name admin-panel \
  -p 127.0.0.1:9090:80 \
  -v /workspace/panel:/usr/share/nginx/html:ro \
  nginx:alpine
docker port admin-panel
```

files.content:
KESTREL ADMIN CONSOLE

Doors, generators, heating.

debrief: Publishing with `-p 9090:80` means every interface; adding a host IP such as `127.0.0.1` narrows who can connect. Pro tip: `docker port <name>` shows the real bindings, which is the quickest way to audit exposure.
